newsitem.title: USA: Citadel promises hazing hearing results Monday.
newsitem.headline: Citadel promises hazing hearing results Monday.

text.p: The Citadel military college said Thursday it would announce on Monday the results of disciplinary hearings for 11 cadets accused of offences linked to the alleged hazing of two women cadets, who quit the school.

In a statement, Citadel spokesman Terry Leedom said the school had hoped to announce the results of the commandant's board sessions and hearings conducted last weekend by March 7. But, he said, "It is now evident that the processes will not be completed by tomorrow."

Three cadets, two seniors and a junior, were charged with violations including physical violence, abusive treatment, failure to report hazing and poor judgment in connection with alleged hazing of Jeanie Mentavlos and Kim Messer, two of the state-funded military school's first women cadets. They could be expelled if found guilty.
Eight other cadets faced lesser charges, including failure to report hazing and sexual harassment.
Messer and Mentavlos withdrew from the Citadel in January, alleging they were victims of severe hazing, physical violence and harassment.
They were among four women enrolled at the school after it changed its all-male admissions policy last summer.
